newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Briton freed on murder charge in Malaysia.
newsitem.headline: Briton freed on murder charge in Malaysia.

text.p: A Malaysian high court on Wednesday gave a British financial consultant and his Filipino bodyguard "a discharge not amounting to an acquittal" on two counts of murder.

Ian Daniel Miller, 48, listed as a consultant at five companies in Malaysia's offshore financial centre on the island of Labuan, and his bodyguard Rikason Alip Tiblan left the court without comment immediately after being freed.
Miller, who owns several nightclubs, and Rikason had been in jail since September 2 awaiting a hearing on the murder charges.
Lawyers said the discharge means that the prosecution did not have enough evidence to convict, but Miller and Tiblan could be picked up any time if fresh evidence against them is found.
The two men faced charges of killing a couple from the Philippines, Erwin Harina and Jocelyn Dumpor, at a house on Labuan island sometime between May 19 and June 14 of this year.
The federal territory of Labuan lies about eight km (five miles) off Kota Kinabalu, capital of Malaysia's north Borneo state of Sabah.
